Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 962dd65e575dde950ef0844568edc37cfb39f302 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Guillaume Giraudon <ggiraudon@prism19.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2022 10:44:28 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: meson-sm1-bananapi-m5: fix wrong GPIO pin
 labeling for CON1

The labels for lines 61 through 84 on the periphs-banks were offset by 2.
2 lines are missing in the BOOT GPIO lines (contains 14, should be 16)
Added 2 empty entries in BOOT to realigned the rest of GPIO labels
to match the Banana Pi M5 schematics.

(Thanks to Neil Armstrong for the heads up on the position of the missing pins)

Fixes: 976e920183e4 ("arm64: dts: meson-sm1: add Banana PI BPI-M5 board dts")
Signed-off-by: Guillaume Giraudon <ggiraudon@prism19.com>
Reviewed-by: Neil Armstrong <narmstrong@baylibre.com>
Signed-off-by: Neil Armstrong <narmstrong@baylibre.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220411144427.874-1-ggiraudon@prism19.com

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/amlogic/meson-sm1-bananapi-m5.dts b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/amlogic/meson-sm1-bananapi-m5.dts
index 5751c48620ed..cadba194b149 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/amlogic/meson-sm1-bananapi-m5.dts
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/amlogic/meson-sm1-bananapi-m5.dts
@@ -437,6 +437,7 @@ &gpio {
 		"",
 		"eMMC_RST#", /* BOOT_12 */
 		"eMMC_DS", /* BOOT_13 */
+		"", "",
 		/* GPIOC */
 		"SD_D0_B", /* GPIOC_0 */
 		"SD_D1_B", /* GPIOC_1 */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/amlogic/meson-sm1-bananapi-m5.dts`**
   - Two empty entries were added to the BOOT GPIO lines to correct the offset in the GPIO pin labeling. This adjustment was made to ensure that the total number of BOOT GPIO lines matches the expected count (from 14 to 16).
   - The specific change involved adding two empty strings (`"", ""`) in the GPIO label list, which realigned the subsequent GPIO labels to match the Banana Pi M5 schematics.

### Relationships
- The modifications in the `.dts` file are directly related to a previous commit identified by the hash `976e920183e4`, which introduced the initial device tree source (DTS) for the Banana Pi M5 board. The current patch addresses a bug in that commit by correcting the GPIO pin labeling, ensuring that the device tree accurately reflects the hardware specifications. The patch also acknowledges the contribution of Neil Armstrong for identifying the issue with the GPIO pin positions.
